extracted.intended_audience: stand-up comedians and performers interested in Stewart Lee–style/meta‑comedy and Brechtian deconstruction
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for creating and evaluating stand-up that deconstructs comedy itself: overtly comments on technique, telegraphs and subverts punchlines, explains jokes at length, and uses Brechtian alienation to make meta-content the source of laughter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core Approach — Deconstruction of comedy
rubrics_metrics.description: Deconstruction of comedy itself. Steps outside material to analyze audience reactions, undermines own punchlines, creates layered self-referential performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The performer intentionally breaks the usual performer-audience illusion to reveal how jokes are constructed and received; aim for layered self-reference rather than straightforward joke-delivery. Use stepping-out moments to create analytic distance and to make form itself the subject.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meta-Humor
rubrics_metrics.description: Openly describes structure and intent of the set while onstage. Abolishes illusion of routines as spontaneous. "I'm doing this kind of joke now" framing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State what you are doing in real time (e.g., 'this is a list bit', 'now I'm doing irony') so the audience is aware of the mechanic; this shifts focus from surprise to process. Anti-pattern: trying to pass meta-commentary off as spontaneous punchlines — the point is explicitness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punchline Subversion
rubrics_metrics.description: Deliberately subverts conventional setup-payoff. Undermines own setups. Extends routines well beyond conventional limits. Forces audiences to reconsider expectations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contradict or invalidate the expected payoff, or extend a setup into repeated or exaggerated territory so the expected release is delayed or transformed. The goal is to make audience expectations the material. Avoid mere confusion without payoff — subversion should lead to a new comic insight or to productive frustration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telegraph the Joke
rubrics_metrics.description: Makes the punchline explicit BEFORE delivery. Telegraphs it long ahead. Defeats the convention of comedy as shock/surprise. Refocuses attention on the journey, not the destination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reveal the anticipated punchline early and repeatedly so the audience follows the build rather than relying on surprise. Use this to highlight mechanics, irony, or to make the eventual payoff about the process. Anti-pattern: telegraphing without craft, which yields predictability with no deeper payoff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain the Joke at Length
rubrics_metrics.description: Spends 20+ minutes explaining a joke. Why it is funny, how it works, what it means. The explanation itself becomes funnier than the joke.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Turn the post-mortem into performance: detailed analysis of a joke's mechanics and meaning can produce comic effect through repetition, escalation, and meta-awareness. Timing and pacing are crucial — the explanation must itself be staged as material, not a lecture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brechtian Influence / Alienation effect (Verfremdungseffekt)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Alienation effect" (Verfremdungseffekt) applied to comedy. Disrupts familiar rhythms of stand-up. Self-reflexivity, slow-paced delivery. Political commentary embedded. Tackles uncomfortable subjects without softening.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use distancing techniques (breaking immersion, slow pacing, explicit commentary on form) to prevent passive consumption and to encourage critical reflection. Can be used to foreground political points or to ask audiences to think about why something is funny. Beware of alienation that only irritates without producing insight or laughter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rubric item: Does the comedian comment on their own technique?
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the comedian comment on their own technique?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for explicit onstage commentary about structure, methods, or intention. This is central to meta-comedy — commentary should be integrated into the act as material, not just as backstage aside.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rubric item: Are conventions deliberately subverted (telegraphed punches, repetition)?
rubrics_metrics.description: Are conventions deliberately subverted (telegraphed punches, repetition)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for intentional use of telegraphing and repetitive extension to upend the usual setup-payoff dynamic. Subversion should be purposeful — used to make the audience re-evaluate expectations or to generate meta-humor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rubric item: Does the comedian extend bits past comfort?
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the comedian extend bits past comfort?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether bits are pushed beyond typical closure points into awkwardness or prolonged repetition to derive absurd insight or to provoke meta-laughter. Extension must be controlled to transform discomfort into comedic material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rubric item: Is there an "alienation" effect (audience pushed out of immersion)?
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there an "alienation" effect (audience pushed out of immersion)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether the performance creates distance so the audience is aware of form/process (e.g., by commenting on the act, slowing delivery, or other Brechtian tactics). The effect should encourage reflection rather than simply breaking tension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rubric item: Does the meta-content itself become the source of humor?
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the meta-content itself become the source of humor?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether commentary about jokes, the comedic form, or the performance mechanics functions as the primary comedic material rather than merely supporting conventional jokes. Success is when explanation, telegraphing, or subversion are funnier than the original punchline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Why It Works (rationale to guide application)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sophisticated audience rewards layered work. The frustration becomes comic. Repetition past comfort = absurd insight. Meta-laughter at the form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this rationale as evaluation: if audience sophistication allows for reward of layers, and if techniques produce productive frustration or absurd insight leading to meta-laughter, the approach is working. If audiences are not engaged by layers, consider adjusting pacing or scaffolding.
